result.title: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation
result.summary: Low-cost arms such as the SO-101 have become the most common entry point to robot learning, yet no released policy performs spatially constrained, language-conditioned tasks on them out of the box, and existing SO-101 benchmarks run only on physical hardware with simple tasks and few held-out objects. We introduce SO-101 Bench, a simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation built on an Isaac Lab digital twin of a real SO-101 setup. It has four tasks scored as five families, 138 objects in seen, unseen-instance and unseen-class splits, 916 evaluation episodes with subsets for held-out appearances, rotate-to-fit planning and occlusion memory, and 3,629 simulated demonstrations on which every learned policy is fine-tuned under an equal compute budget. The twin ranks policies as the real robot does: five policies trained without real data, four VLAs and an LLM agent, keep their exact ranking when the same weights run on the physical arm in an unseen environment with unseen objects (Spearman rho = 1.00, MMRV = 0.000), although simulation overestimates success. Across nine VLAs and world-action models, the best learned policies score near 61%, with spatial placement, unseen object classes and rotate-to-fit planning remaining open. An LLM agent that writes code and hands grasping to a learned policy scores 83.2%, and an ablation shows that this lead comes from the choice of harness and the choice of language model.

AI.brief_summary: 构建基于真实 SO-101 数字孪生的仿真基准，用四类任务、138 个物体与 916 个评估回合考察语言条件下的空间操作，验证仿真与真机策略排序一致（ρ=1.00），并显示最佳 VLA 约 61%，而「写代码 + 学习抓取策略」的 LLM agent 达 83.2%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其中的遮挡记忆与 rotate-to-fit 子集需要跨时间维持空间信息，且外层 LLM harness 与学习策略分工带来大幅增益，可供核查「latent 状态 vs 外部工具/代码」的职责划分，但属具身操作设定，与 LVR 内部表示无直接检验。
